sections.html:
The Logan County recorder sits in the annex at 100 S. Madriver Street, Bellefontaine, OH 43311. Call 937-599-7201. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 until 4:30, and Wednesday is the day it issues Veteran ID cards.

The recorder keeps the land ownership record and every lien against land. Each filing is stored in archival form and indexed so a searcher can trace ownership forward in time. Title examiners, attorneys, genealogists and historians all use those files.

The Logan Online portal has a Recorder's Document Search for looking up filed documents. The recorder also publishes Document Standardization Guidelines, a historical page and a Veteran ID Card Program page.

A short schedule appears on the county's recordable documents page. Everything the recorder collects goes into the county general fund. Phone 937-599-7201 for a total on a lengthy document.

Logan County recording fees
ChargeFee
First 2 pages$39
Each additional page$8
Non-standardization fee$20
Marginal reference, each$4

sections.h2: Layout rules that trigger the $20 fee
sections.html:
The extra $20 applies to paper that ignores Ohio Revised Code 317.114. The county's guidelines tie the rule to documents prepared after June 30, 2009, and spell out the specifications:

  • Type no smaller than 10 point.
  • Sheets between letter size and legal size, meaning 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Ink in black or blue, with no highlighter marks.
  • One inch of white space along both sides and the foot of each page.
  • Three inches blank at the head of page one, held for stamps from the recorder, auditor and engineer.
  • An inch and a half blank at the head of every later page.

Five categories fall outside the rule: papers from a court or a taxing authority, plats, DD-214 discharge forms, state or federal documents, and anything signed before the law took effect. The county also offers a downloadable template, which saves a title agent the trouble of guessing at margins.

sections.h2: The auditor comes before the recorder
sections.html:
A deed visits the county auditor first, and that office shares the 100 S. Madriver Street address. The auditor's forms page lists the paperwork that can come into play:

  • Conveyance Form DTE 100 for an ordinary sale, and DTE 100M for a manufactured home.
  • Exempt Conveyance DTE 100EX, or 100MEX for a manufactured home.
  • Agriculture Conveyance DTE 102.
  • Homestead Conveyance DTE 101.
  • Owner Occupied Credit Application DTE 105C and the Homestead Exemption Application DTE 105A.
  • Destroyed Property Application DTE 26 for a building that no longer stands.

Logan County also posts a Survey and Conveyance Standards PDF for legal descriptions and an online Conveyance Fee Calculator. The state conveyance fee falls on the grantor under section 319.202. A county transfer tax joins it only where commissioners adopted one under Chapter 322. The auditor can say which charges apply to your sale.

sections.h2: Forfeited land sales and the recorder
sections.html:
A parcel that went through tax foreclosure and drew no buyer in two offerings is forfeited to the State of Ohio and remanded to the auditor. The auditor's auction rules describe a sale at the Logan County Courthouse Annex, 100 S. Madriver Street. Properties sell "As-Is" and "Buyer Beware," and the auditor makes no representation about possession, eviction or prior inspection.

The high bidder gets an Auditor's Deed. The auditor files it with the recorder and delivers it to the purchaser, and ownership passes at the moment the deed is delivered to the recorder. That deed extinguishes earlier title except for taxes and assessments not yet due, federal tax liens, easements and covenants running with the land. A delinquent taxpayer or a current owner of the parcel cannot buy.

Bidders pay everything or leave at least $1,000 per parcel on sale day, and the remainder is due within 10 calendar days. The auction rules add a 50 cent per parcel transfer charge and a 50 cent per parcel charge for envelope and postage, on top of recording.

The treasurer's office sits at 100 S. Madriver Street, Suite D, and answers at (937) 599-7223 on weekdays between 8:00 AM and 4:30 PM. The second-half bill is due each July. An automatic withdrawal option pulls the bill from a bank account on the last due date.

The county follows a six-year cycle: a reappraisal every six years, and a possible adjustment in the third calendar year after it. Taxable value is 35 percent of appraised value. The state schedule puts Logan County in a 2028 update and a 2031 reappraisal.

Challenging your value

Formal complaints go to the Board of Revision, which accepts them from January 1 through March 31. The board has three seats: the auditor, the treasurer and the president of the commissioners, or their representatives. An owner can bring appraisals or comparable sales to the hearing.

Logan County lies in west central Ohio, and Bellefontaine is the seat and only city. Population reached 46,302 in July 2025. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $203,200, and 77.6 percent of housing is owner-occupied. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,326 a month, and median gross rent is $845. The county had 24,071 housing units in July 2025.

sections.h2: The recorder's role and Torrens land
sections.html:
Every Ohio county has had a recorder since the Northwest Territory of 1787. Voters have chosen the office since 1829, and a four-year term has applied since 1936.

The recorder also handles Torrens registration. Where land is registered under the Torrens Act, its boundaries are certified and a state insurance fund backs the title, and the recorder keeps those registered land records. A seller who owns an unusual rural tract should ask the Logan recorder whether any part of it was registered.

The auditor, the treasurer and the recorder all list 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine as their address, so a closing agent can take the transfer, the tax question and the recording to one building.

Typical order of a sale

The title company drafts the deed and both sides sign. The deed goes to the auditor for the conveyance form and fee, then across the building to the recorder. A seller should confirm with the treasurer that nothing is owed on the parcel before closing, since taxes follow the property.

Before you drive over, check the document against the layout list above: type size, margins, ink color and the blank space at the top of each page. Bring the fee for the page count, and call 937-599-7201 if the deed runs long and you want a total in advance. A cash sale that closes without a lender skips the payoff release, which leaves one fewer paper to record.

faqs.q: What is the filing fee for a short Logan County deed?
faqs.a: The posted schedule charges $39 for the opening two pages, then $8 for every page after that. A document that misses the layout standards picks up $20 more.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Logan County recorder?
faqs.a: The office at 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine opens weekdays at 8:00 and closes at 4:30. Its phone number is 937-599-7201.

faqs.q: Which papers skip the Logan County layout fee?
faqs.a: Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD-214 discharge forms and state or federal documents are exempt, along with anything executed before the law began.

faqs.q: Does the Logan County recorder help fill out deed forms?
faqs.a: The office keeps and indexes records. Have a title company or attorney draft the deed, and phone 937-599-7201 with filing questions.

faqs.q: When does a forfeited land buyer own the property in Logan County?
faqs.a: Ownership passes when the auditor hands the Auditor's Deed to the recorder. The auditor then sends the recorded deed to the purchaser.
